brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Stagewell, the feature-flag and gradual-rollout service in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: calm, precise and trustworthy for platform teams who ship to millions of users; not playful. No toggles, switches, flags, rockets or traffic lights. Web app, docs site, GitHub avatar and a VS Code extension icon.

claim.notes: Five concepts across two rounds all failed the critic gate (blind averages 4.2, 4.2 and 5.2; two others were struck at sketch review), so nothing was finalized, exported or gallery-built.

concepts.title: Guarded Block
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a square in code brackets [■] - camera focus box / code editor icon; struck. s2 a battery on its side (tall body bracket, square, small terminal nub) or a plug - battery was an earlier failure; struck. s3 a letter C / box with a drawer sliding out - reads as an export or eject UI icon and a different letter; struck. s4 [ ] brackets with a square pushing through a broken right bracket - still the code/viewfinder icon, plus a cut-bracket device, and at 16 px it reads '[:' ; struck. Every variant collapses to brackets, and square brackets around anything are UI/code geometry for this audience. Different move: drop brackets entirely. Express 'guarded release' as one closed, calm form - e.g. a solid block partly enclosed by a single continuous wall with one deliberate opening (a sheltered interior counter, not a frame), or merge the effort into two-wells (contained, held safely). Avoid stairs, fills that read as gauges, rings and frames.

concepts.title: Stepped Double-l
readsAs: the word 'stagewe' followed by a stray glyph (a 4, an h or a Cyrillic ch)
a Z-shaped stair bracket or Tetris-like step piece
a Hebrew or Armenian letter -- worst case the audience reads the product name as misspelled or truncated
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 two offset bars / broken glyph (offset-cut device); s2 a single stair stroke descending, second read lightning bolt at 16 px; s3 pause button (struck, UI icon); s4 a block split by a jogging seam, reads as broken H (cut device). Pick s2: one continuous stroke with a landing is the only sketch that says stages without a cut. Fix: kill the lightning-bolt reading (landing must be clearly horizontal and longer, ends square, no diagonal feel at 16 px); give it a distinctive proportion or terminal so it is not a generic stair glyph; consider a non-green accent to separate from a plain teal tile; test on dark and in a tab.

concepts.title: Stepped Well
readsAs: a descending stair/bar chart falling into a cup
a low-battery or fill-level indicator with an orange bar
a factory or building silhouette -- worst case a declining-metrics chart for a product whose job is protecting error rates
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 stairs descending into a pool/vessel in section, with a lit floor slab - closest to the idea; s2 a hamburger menu / text-align / letter E icon, struck (UI icon); s3 a black ball with a stepped slot, reads as a coin bank or Pac-Man-like bite, mushy at 16 px; s4 a letter U / magnet / molar tooth, struck (different letter). Pick s1. Keep: side-on section, uneven terraces, amber on the lowest floor. Fix: (1) the outer frame reads as a U or a bin - thicken and square the right wall so it reads as solid ground, not a container; (2) the left-only stair risks 'swimming pool ladder' and descending bar chart - make treads deep and few (3), uneven rise, and vary the right wall so the void is a cut into ground; (3) the amber slab currently sits like a progress bar/water line - give it a gap from the walls (tool warns block and lit overlap and merge in one colour) and make it a tread, not a stripe; (4) keep amber small, no dot.

concepts.title: Two Wells
readsAs: a lowercase W monogram (two U cups joined)
a shot glass or pint of beer dropped into a cup
a molar tooth / two rounded bowls
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a rounded W with slightly uneven valleys - the depth difference reads as wobbly type, not two wells; idea invisible. s2 a snaking stroke / sine wave or 'lu' - wave reading and not an instant w in the word; struck. s3 a W with one trough clipped - reads as a cut letter, flat troughs feel mechanical, idea invisible. s4 a W with amber liquid standing in the left valley - the only sketch where 'well' (something held, safely contained) is legible at first look; pick. Fixes: (1) the amber must read as liquid with a flat level surface well below the valley's top, not as a filled U - right now the fill traces the whole bottom curve and can read as a separate orange 'u' or a gauge/battery level (earlier failure); (2) leave a clear gap between fill and stroke so one-color versions survive (designer warning); (3) keep the w otherwise identical to the wordmark's other letters - test 'stagewell' set in full at 16 px and 24 px and confirm it reads instantly, not 'stageUwell' or a highlighted letter gimmick; (4) drop the unequal-depth asymmetry unless it reads as intent; (5) standalone icon must not look like a cup, a heart or a generic 'W with dot'. Risk: single-letter-with-accent-colour is a common wordmark device; the fill shape must be ownable.

concepts.title: Widening Field
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a wifi/signal quarter-fan (radiating arcs from a corner), struck; s2 a volume/speaker or megaphone icon (small tip, taller slanted bars), also an ascending bar chart, struck; s3 a folding hand fan / bar-chart of growing blades from a pivot, struck. All three are still a radiating-from-a-point fan; the 'widening' metaphor keeps landing on signal and sound icons. A rework of the fan will not pass. If this concept continues, abandon the radial origin entirely: try widening expressed as a single solid plane (e.g. a parallelogram/trapezoid slab whose top edge steps out in uneven increments, no gaps between bands, no point of origin), or retire the concept in favour of stepped-well.
